subject.title: [Bug] Dashboard Stop button can corrupt session files + agent permission isolation lacks guardrails

question: Should OpenClaw keep the trusted single-operator host-exec model for per-agent state access, or introduce a core per-agent filesystem/approval boundary while separately fixing Stop/session durability?
rationale: Current docs and code intentionally allow full/off host exec in one Gateway trust domain, so changing per-agent state protection affects the product security boundary and compatibility for existing operators.

options.title: Split And Fix Stop Durability First
options.body: Track Stop cancellation, JSONL drain, and recovery as a core data-loss bug while moving per-agent exec isolation to a separate security-boundary design item.

options.title: Tighten Per-Agent Exec Boundaries
options.body: Define a new default or migration path that denies or approval-gates sibling agent state access, with docs and upgrade proof for existing full/off users.

options.title: Keep Current Exec Trust Model
options.body: Close or narrow the per-agent isolation request as unsupported under the current single-operator Gateway model, while still requiring the Stop/session corruption fix.

recommendation.title: Split And Fix Stop Durability First
recommendation.body: Track Stop cancellation, JSONL drain, and recovery as a core data-loss bug while moving per-agent exec isolation to a separate security-boundary design item.

likelyOwner.reason: History and adjacent maintainer comments tie this decision to the current host-exec trust model and chat-abort lifecycle ownership.
